_about.rule: A verdict of keep, revise or remove rests on a source fetched on the date above (sourceUrl), or — only where the entry says so in `change` — on the product's own code read and run that day. Everything else is "unverified — needs a local clinician"; for those, `leaning` holds the direction a clinician is asked to confirm and is NOT a decision.

fields.tools[].class: base = every role; specialty = the listed roles only
fields.tools[].screenName: the name on screen in en-US; for a slot (never shown) a plain description
fields.addTools[].verifiedToday: true = a US source naming the tool was fetched on the date above; false = named from general knowledge only, needs a local clinician
fields.addTools[].formulaSourceUrl: a URL only where one was fetched; otherwise null and `formulaSource` carries the citation as far as it was read
fields.specialties[].tools: "@core" = every tool of `coreSet`; other entries are keys of `tools` or ids of `addTools`

SAFETY. (1) The referral flags are labelled "KDIGO criterion" but do not match the KDIGO 2024 list read today. KDIGO 2024 lists, among others: eGFR below 30; a sustained fall in GFR of more than 20%; albumin-to-creatinine ratio of 300 mg/g or more together with hematuria; a ratio consistently above 700 mg/g; a 5-year kidney-failure risk of 3 to 5% by a validated equation. The tool instead flags any ratio above 300 mg/g alone, a fall of more than 25% in a year, and "the very-high-risk cell" — the last is not on KDIGO's list at all. (2) With no albumin result typed, the tool still shows a risk colour, silently treating the patient as category A1: eGFR 75 with no urine test reads "Low risk (green cell)". The cell needs both values; with one missing the tool should show the GFR category only. (3) A ratio of exactly 300 mg/g is called A2; the two KDIGO/KDOQI texts read today write the severe category as "300 mg/g or more". The category table itself could not be read: a nephrologist settles the boundary. (4) The tool asks the doctor to type eGFR: add the US equation (CKD-EPI 2021, see the core set). Units (mg/g; mL/min/1.73 m²) are right for the US. Show it also to family medicine, endocrinology and cardiology.
tools.licence: unclear — KDIGO's categories are widely reproduced; the guideline text and heat-map figure are KDIGO's copyright (terms not read)

MISLEADING HERE. The tool calls any average up to 25 dB "Within normal limits". The American Speech-Language-Hearing Association's table, from the very paper the tool cites (Clark 1981), has Normal up to 15 dB and a separate "Slight" loss from 16 to 25 dB: a 20 dB average is reported as normal where the US reference calls it a slight hearing loss (it matters most in children). Add the "Slight" grade. Not verified today: which frequencies make up the average in US practice (the tool uses 0.5, 1, 2 and 4 kHz), and the 10 dB and 15 dB flags. The audiologist role should see this tool too; today only otolaryngology does.

tools.screenName: Expected height from the parents' heights
tools.change: The correction is the one US family doctors are taught: 13 cm (5 in). The RANGE is not: the tool shows 8.5 cm either side (a 1970 British paper); the American Academy of Family Physicians' journal says most children end up "within 10 cm (4 in), or two standard deviations" of the figure. For 64 in and 70 in parents of a boy the tool shows 66.2 to 72.9 in where the US source gives about 65.6 to 73.5 in. Make the range a number the country states. Heights must also be typed in feet and inches (a kit gap already recorded by the earlier audit). Show it to family medicine as well.

LICENCE AND LAW. (1) BI-RADS is a registered trademark of the American College of Radiology and its atlas is copyrighted; ACR says commercial software needs a copyright licensing agreement. Take the BI-RADS names off the screen until that agreement exists. (2) For mammography, federal rules (21 CFR 900.12) fix the wording of the final assessment in words, not numbers (seven statements, one of them for a mammogram done after a marker is placed), two separate "Incomplete" statements, and a breast-density statement in every report. The tool shows bare numbers 0 to 6, one incomplete category and no density. (3) ACR now publishes a v2025 manual; the tool cites the 2013 edition.
tools.licence: needs permission — ACR licence agreement for commercial software
